Ph.D. Admission & How to Apply
Ph.D. Admissions & How to Apply
Application Deadline: December 1
Applications to the Ph.D. program in Ecology and Evolution are evaluated holistically
according to multiple criteria, including academic preparation, scholarly potential,
commitment to an inclusive learning environment, program alignment, and written communication.
Before You Apply: Contacting Faculty Advisors
Prior to submitting an application, prospective students are strongly advised to contact
faculty members whose research aligns with their interests. Most inquiries begin in
the summer preceding the application deadline.
Review research interests and recent publications on our Program Faculty Directory.
Contact 1–2 potential advisors with a detailed description of your specific research
interests, educational background, and relevant technical skills or experience.
Ask if the faculty member is accepting new Ph.D. students.
Note: While students are admitted to the program as a whole rather than specific labs,
prior contact with and support from a potential advisor substantially strengthens
an application. For general advice on navigating graduate school applications, review
the Bulletin of the Ecological Society of America. Potential applicants are also encourged to reach out to current doctoral students,
particularly members of the labs under consideration.
How to Apply & Required Components
Applications must be submitted online via the Stony Brook Graduate School Application Portal. A complete application includes:
Graduate School Application Form: Includes general contact information, educational background, proposed advisors,
and interest in internal fellowships.
Statement of Purpose: The statement of purpose helps the admissoins committee understand your academic
objectives and helps us determine if you are a good match for the program. In your
statement of purpose: (1) clearly articulate specific examples of the types of research
questions that interest you (understanding that these may evolve), (2) describe how
your background makes you a good fit for the Ecology & Evolution program and to the
lab(s) to which you are applying, (3) summarize your research experience, highlighting
any presentations, publications or awards, (4) describe your potential for contributing
to an inclusive learning environment, as evidence by life experience, participation
or leadership in affinity groups, mentoring, tutoring, outreach or volunteer experience.
Curriculum Vitae (CV): Your CV summarizes your academic and work experiences. Be sure to include previous
education, presentations, publications, academic honors, teaching experience, professional
experience, leadership and volunteer experience, skills and certifications. A helpful
guide to preparing an effective CV can be found here. An alternate guide can be found at this link.
Transcripts: Official or unofficial academic transcripts (including GPA) from all college-level
institutions attended. Transcripts are used as evidence of academic preparation.
Three Letters of Recommendation: Request letters from former professors, employers, or research supervisors who can
address your research potential, academic preparation, and character.
TOEFL / IELTS Scores: Required for applicants whose primary language is not English.
Application Fee & Waivers: The application fee is $100. Applications will not be processed without the fee.
Review Fee Waiver Eligibility Criteria for options based on financial need, military service, CIE recruitment event participation,
or designated opportunity programs.
Interview Process
Short remote interviews are conducted for a subset of applicants to evaluate characteristics
critical to graduate success, including curiosity, perseverance, independence, maturity,
and oral communication skills. These evaluations are conducted by the admissions committee
with input from potential advisors.
